result.create: Explicit user request required; Git projects default to worktree; optional existing branch or working-tree starting state

result.message: Background follow-up to an existing task
result.wait: Wait for first completion/input-required among up to eight targets; cursor suppresses delivered final
result.handoff: Move another task and associated Git state between checkout and Codex worktree; calling task cannot move itself
result.archive: Archive or unarchive a task in the background

capabilities.claim: In the current Desktop session, list can locate this active project task and read returns its task identity/status, while a nonexistent thread ID produces an explicit not-found failure.
limitations: No reliability rate or archived/paginated/stale-host behavior established
Does not imply mutation or coordination capabilities
capabilities.failure_policy: Treat not-found and host mismatch as explicit failures; never infer success from an empty task result.

capabilities.claim: The current Desktop tool schema can create a user-owned project task in a Codex-managed worktree from the default branch, an existing branch, or the current working tree.
conditions: User explicitly requests a new task
Saved project is a Git repository
Target host supports the requested starting state
limitations: Default HEAD/branch/detached behavior not observed
Dirty, ignored, submodule, LFS, and failure recovery not observed
capabilities.failure_policy: Do not create a test task without explicit user authorization; do not infer copied state from the tool call alone.

capabilities.claim: The current Desktop tool schema can fork completed task history into a child that uses the same directory.
conditions: Fork environment is same-directory or omitted
limitations: Exact completed-history cutoff not observed
Concurrent file visibility and write collision behavior not observed
capabilities.failure_policy: Treat same-directory forks as unsafe for overlapping writes until an isolated fixture demonstrates the boundary.

capabilities.claim: The current Desktop tool schema can fork a Codex task into a child whose setup uses a worktree.
limitations: Starting revision, branch identity, setup failure, and cleanup are not observed
capabilities.failure_policy: Do not assign mutable files until the child workspace and base revision are independently confirmed.

capabilities.claim: The current Desktop tool schema can send a background follow-up prompt to an existing task.
limitations: Delivery, ordering, duplication, persistence, and active-turn behavior are not currently observed
capabilities.failure_policy: Use messages as control signals; require artifact/revision evidence before accepting state changes.

capabilities.claim: The current Desktop tool schema can wait on up to eight tasks and uses cursors to suppress previously delivered final text.
conditions: Target identities and optional host IDs resolve
limitations: Timeout, error, input-required, commentary, and stale-cursor behavior are not observed
capabilities.failure_policy: Do not interpret timeout or omitted final text as task success.

capabilities.claim: The current Desktop tool schema can move another task and associated Git state between its checkout and a Codex worktree on the current host.
conditions: Target is another local Codex task
The caller is not handing off itself
limitations: Dirty/untracked/submodule/LFS/conflict behavior and recovery are not observed
Tool completion does not prove destination understanding
capabilities.failure_policy: Destination must recheck cwd, HEAD, status, artifact hashes, and unresolved risks before continuing.

capabilities.claim: The current Desktop tool schema can archive or unarchive a Codex task in the background.
limitations: Relationship between archive state and managed worktree retention is not observed
capabilities.failure_policy: Never treat archive as authorization or evidence that a worktree was deleted.

capabilities.claim: The current task exposes spawn, follow-up, message, interrupt, list, and wait operations for session-scoped subagents that share the filesystem.
conditions: Current collaboration policy permits the requested subagent action
limitations: Context inheritance, cwd, nested spawn, write visibility, interruption, and cleanup are not observed
Feature flag stability does not prove lifecycle semantics
capabilities.failure_policy: Use explicit ownership and independently verify outputs; do not infer workspace isolation.
